name: Brendan Eich
milestone_by_age_26: No material milestone by age 26 found; earned MS in computer science (1985, age ~24) and worked on OS/network code at Silicon Graphics, but his defining achievement—creating JavaScript at Netscape—came in 1995 at age 33–34.
early_history_summary: Raised in Pittsburgh, Gaithersburg, and Palo Alto; graduated Cubberley High (1979), BA math/CS from Santa Clara University, MS from University of Illinois Urbana-Champaign (1985). Spent seven years at Silicon Graphics on systems code before Netscape.
family_context_summary: Not documented in reviewed sources beyond Irish-German ancestry and Roman Catholic background.
evidence_summary: Brendan Eich completed graduate CS training by his mid-twenties and built systems experience at Silicon Graphics, but the milestone that defines his career—inventing JavaScript in ten days at Netscape in 1995—occurred at age 33–34. Co-founding Mozilla and later Brave also came well after age 26. No independently verifiable material breakthrough by 26 was found.

name: Bjarne Stroustrup
milestone_by_age_26: No material milestone by age 26 found; earned Cand.scient. in math/CS from Aarhus University (1975, age ~24) and was a Cambridge PhD student, but began developing C++ ("C with Classes") only after joining Bell Labs in 1979 at age 28–29.
early_history_summary: Born working-class in Aarhus, Denmark; attended Aarhus University 1969–1975 and learned object-oriented ideas from Kristen Nygaard's visits. Completed PhD at Cambridge under David Wheeler in 1979, then joined Bell Labs.
family_context_summary: Working-class family in Aarhus, Denmark; attended local schools.
evidence_summary: Stroustrup completed a strong European CS education by his mid-twenties and was pursuing a Cambridge PhD, but C++ design and implementation began at Bell Labs in 1979 when he was about 28. Public release of C++ and The C++ Programming Language textbook came in 1985 (age ~34). No material language-creation or industry milestone by age 26 was found.

name: Dennis Ritchie
milestone_by_age_26: No material milestone by age 26 found; Harvard degrees in physics and applied mathematics (1963) and joined Bell Labs Computing Science Research Center in 1967 (age 25–26), but Unix (~1969) and the C language (early 1970s) were developed after age 26.
early_history_summary: Born in Bronxville, New York; father was Bell Labs scientist Alistair E. Ritchie. Grew up in Summit, New Jersey; Summit High School; Harvard physics and applied math (1963). Drafted PhD thesis on computational complexity but never officially received the degree.
family_context_summary: Father Alistair E. Ritchie was a longtime Bell Labs scientist and co-author of The Design of Switching Circuits; family lived in Summit, New Jersey.
parent_family_domain_summary: Father was a Bell Labs switching-circuit scientist, providing direct domain proximity to industrial research computing.
evidence_summary: Ritchie entered Bell Labs around age 25–26 with a Harvard background and family proximity to Bell research culture, but co-creating Unix with Ken Thompson (~1969, age ~27–28) and inventing C (early 1970s) occurred after 26. Starting a research job is not treated as the material milestone under a strict age-26 rule.

name: Stewart Butterfield
milestone_by_age_26: No material milestone by age 26 found; BA philosophy (University of Victoria, 1996) and MPhil (Cambridge, 1998, age ~25), then Gradfinder.com around 2000 (age ~26–27). Flickr (2004, age 31) and Slack (2013, age 40) arrived later.
early_history_summary: Born Dharma Jeremy Butterfield in Lund, British Columbia; spent early childhood on a commune without running water or electricity after his father fled the Vietnam draft. Family moved to Victoria at age five; self-taught coding; BA philosophy UVic (1996), MPhil Clare College Cambridge (1998).
family_context_summary: Grew up partly on a remote Canadian commune without electricity or running water; father had fled the US Vietnam draft; later middle-class life in Victoria, BC.
parent_family_domain_summary: Not documented as tech/business domain experts.
evidence_summary: Butterfield finished elite philosophy training by ~25 and joined Gradfinder.com around 2000, but the dated material successes that define him—co-founding Flickr (2004) and Slack (2013)—came at ages 31 and 40. Gradfinder is not treated as a clear material breakout under a conservative age-26 bar.

name: Cal Henderson
milestone_by_age_26: Served as chief software architect of Flickr (launched 2004; Yahoo acquisition 2005) at age ~23, after co-owning creative community B3ta and building City Creator (~2003, age 22); later co-founded Tiny Speck/Slack.
early_history_summary: British software engineer; attended Sharnbrook Upper School and graduated software engineering from Birmingham City University (2002, age 21). Built fan site for Ludicorp's Game Neverending and was hired by Stewart Butterfield; became Flickr's chief software architect while still in his early twenties.
primary_early_advantage_tags: early web community B3ta, Flickr infrastructure, Web 2.0 wave, Butterfield partnership, open-source contributor
evidence_summary: Cal Henderson graduated software engineering at 21, co-owned the UK creative community B3ta, and shipped City Creator (~2003). He broke into Ludicorp via a fan site and became Flickr's chief software architect by his early twenties, building scalable photo-sharing infrastructure on the Web 2.0 wave. He later co-founded Tiny Speck with Butterfield, which pivoted to Slack. Early advantage was primarily scarce systems skill plus high-trust cofounder partnership and early online community distribution, not family capital.
starting_point: Not documented in reviewed sources beyond UK origin and software-engineering education at Birmingham City University.
current_position: Co-founder of Slack; longtime CTO who helped build the product sold to Salesforce for $27.7 billion; San Francisco-based engineering leader and author of Building Scalable Web Sites.

trajectory.event: Graduated software engineering from Birmingham City University and was active in early web communities including B3ta.
Shipped City Creator, a web project featured in Yahoo! picks, and worked as technical director of special web projects at EMAP.
Served as chief software architect of Flickr at Ludicorp as the photo-sharing product launched into the Web 2.0 wave.
Flickr acquired by Yahoo; continued leading engineering through the acquisition integration.
Published Building Scalable Web Sites with O'Reilly Media, codifying lessons from Flickr-scale systems.
Co-founded Tiny Speck with Stewart Butterfield as VP of engineering after Glitch game work began.
Tiny Speck's internal tooling launched publicly as Slack, which became a dominant workplace collaboration product.
Salesforce announced acquisition of Slack Technologies for approximately $27.7 billion.

name: Biz Stone
milestone_by_age_26: No clearly material independent milestone by age 26 found; was creative director at Xanga (1999–2001, age ~25–27) after being invited by friends who started the company, then book design and blogging work. Defining co-founding of Twitter came in 2006 at age 32.
early_history_summary: Born Christopher Isaac Stone in Boston; Wellesley High School; attended Northeastern and UMass Boston without graduating. Left school to design book covers at Little, Brown; taught himself web design; joined early blogging platform Xanga as creative director.
family_context_summary: Not documented in reviewed sources beyond Boston/Wellesley, Massachusetts upbringing.
evidence_summary: Stone left college for design work and became creative director at Xanga around age 25 after friends invited him to join their early blogging startup. That role is real but is treated conservatively as employment rather than a clear founding breakout. Twitter (2006, age 32), Google/Blogger leadership, and later Jelly define his fame and came after 26.

name: Chad Hurley
milestone_by_age_26: No material milestone by age 26 found; BA fine art from Indiana University of Pennsylvania (1999, age 22) and design work at PayPal (including the original logo), but co-founding YouTube occurred in 2005 at age 28.
early_history_summary: Born in Reading, Pennsylvania; raised near Birdsboro; Twin Valley High School (cross-country state titles, Technology Student Association); BA fine art IUP 1999. Joined eBay's PayPal division as a designer after college, meeting future YouTube cofounders Steve Chen and Jawed Karim.
family_context_summary: Second child of Don and Joann Hurley; grew up near Birdsboro, Pennsylvania with siblings Heather and Brent.
parent_family_domain_summary: Not documented as tech-domain experts in reviewed sources.
evidence_summary: Hurley completed a fine-art degree at 22 and did product/UI design at PayPal, including logo work, through his mid-twenties. The material founding event—YouTube in 2005 with Chen and Karim, sold to Google for $1.65B in 2006—came at age 28. PayPal employment is not counted as a defining breakout by 26.

name: Ben Silbermann
milestone_by_age_26: No material milestone by age 26 found; Yale political science (2003), Google ads group job, and failed iPhone app Tote preceded Pinterest, which launched in March 2010 when he was 27.
early_history_summary: Born in Iowa (1982) to ophthalmologist parents Jane Wang and Neil Silbermann; Des Moines Central Academy and Roosevelt High (1999); Research Science Institute at MIT (1998); Yale BA political science (2003). Worked in Google online advertising before leaving to build iPhone apps.
family_context_summary: Raised in Des Moines, Iowa by ophthalmologist parents Jane Wang and Neil Silbermann (Chinese and German descent) with a family eye practice in Urbandale.
parent_family_domain_summary: Parents were ophthalmologists—professional but not tech/product domain experts.
evidence_summary: Silbermann had elite education (RSI, Yale) and a Google ads stint by his mid-twenties, plus an unsuccessful collector app (Tote). Pinterest was founded/launched around 2009–2010 when he was already 27. Under a strict age-26 cutoff, no material breakout is dated before that.

name: Tony Xu
milestone_by_age_26: No material milestone by age 26 found; UC Berkeley industrial engineering, McKinsey/eBay/PayPal roles, and Stanford MBA (2013) led to co-founding DoorDash in 2013 at approximately age 28–29 (sources place birth in 1983/1984).
early_history_summary: Born Xu Xun in Nanjing, China; immigrated to Champaign, Illinois at about age four. Mother Julie Cao opened acupuncture clinics after working restaurant jobs; father earned a PhD in aerospace engineering/applied math at Illinois. BS industrial engineering/OR from UC Berkeley; MBA Stanford GSB 2013.
family_context_summary: Chinese immigrant family; mother was a Chinese-trained doctor who later ran acupuncture clinics and had worked restaurant jobs; father was an academic who completed a PhD at UIUC.
parent_family_domain_summary: Mother's restaurant work later informed DoorDash's small-business delivery thesis; parents were not tech founders.
evidence_summary: Xu's immigrant path, Berkeley engineering degree, consulting experience, and Stanford MBA set him up for founding, but DoorDash (and PaloAltoDelivery.com in 2012) were founded when he was already past 26. IPO fame and billionaire status arrived in 2020 around age 36. No dated material breakout by age 26 was found.

name: Andy Fang
milestone_by_age_26: Co-founded DoorDash in 2013 at age ~21 while a Stanford computer-science student and served as founding CTO (2013–2019), building the core logistics platform that later IPO'd and made him a billionaire.
early_history_summary: Born 1992 in San Jose to Taiwanese immigrant parents; one of four children. Graduated The Harker School (2010), then Stanford BS computer science. Roomed with Stanley Tang as a freshman; met Tony Xu in a joint engineering-business course; founded DoorDash as a class project (initially PaloAltoDelivery.com).
family_context_summary: Taiwanese American family in San Jose Bay Area; parents immigrated from Taiwan; one of four children.
parent_family_domain_summary: Not documented as tech founders; immigrant professional/family context in Silicon Valley geography.
primary_early_advantage_tags: Stanford CS, Harker School, Silicon Valley, DoorDash cofounder trio, on-demand delivery wave
evidence_summary: Andy Fang co-founded DoorDash at ~21 as Stanford CS student and founding CTO, shipping the technical core while the founders personally made deliveries. Elite prep (Harker) and Stanford plus Bay Area geography and a tight cofounder team (Tang, Xu) compounded on the on-demand logistics wave. Family background is Taiwanese immigrant San Jose; no strong documented parental tech apprenticeship, so peer team and institutional pipeline dominate.
starting_point: Born 1992 in San Jose, California to Taiwanese immigrant parents; raised in the Bay Area and educated at The Harker School before Stanford.
current_position: DoorDash co-founder and head of consumer engineering; owns roughly 4% of the company; net worth on the order of $1–2B; married tennis player Carol Zhao (2024).

trajectory.event: Graduated The Harker School and entered Stanford University for computer science.
Co-founded DoorDash (from PaloAltoDelivery.com class project) with Tony Xu and Stanley Tang and became founding CTO.
DoorDash scaled nationally; Fang and Tang named to Forbes 30 Under 30 Consumer Technology.
Stepped down as CTO (February 2019) while remaining a core technical leader and board-level cofounder.
DoorDash IPO; Fang became a billionaire as the stock soared on debut.
Continues as head of consumer engineering and major shareholder; Forbes lists him among richest under-40 self-made billionaires.

name: Stanley Tang
milestone_by_age_26: Co-founded DoorDash in 2013 at age ~20–21 while at Stanford; earlier published Amazon bestseller eMillions: Behind-the-Scenes Stories of 14 Successful Internet Millionaires at age 15–16 (~2008).
early_history_summary: Born 1992 in Sendai, Japan; raised in Hong Kong (King George V School, Kowloon). Began computing around age three, launched web products as a teen, published eMillions as a high-schooler, then moved to the Bay Area for Stanford CS (graduated 2014). Brief Facebook software-engineering stint in 2012 before DoorDash.
family_context_summary: Born in Japan, raised in Hong Kong; Hong Kong-American identity. Specific parental occupations not detailed in reviewed sources.
primary_early_advantage_tags: teen internet entrepreneurship, eMillions bestseller, Stanford CS, DoorDash cofounder trio, on-demand delivery wave
evidence_summary: Stanley Tang accumulated unusual early reps—coding from childhood, teen web products, and an Amazon bestseller on internet millionaires at ~15—before co-founding DoorDash at ~21 with Stanford peers Andy Fang and Tony Xu. Stanford and Bay Area placement plus a durable cofounder team accelerated the on-demand delivery wave. Family domain advantage is not well documented; the dominant pattern is self-created early specialization.
starting_point: Born 1992 in Sendai, Japan and raised in Hong Kong; attended King George V School before moving to California for Stanford.
current_position: DoorDash co-founder, chief product officer / director-level operator and major shareholder; net worth around $1B; married Gloria Zhu (2023); private pilot and poker player.

trajectory.event: Published Amazon bestseller eMillions: Behind-the-Scenes Stories of 14 Successful Internet Millionaires while still in high school in Hong Kong.
Moved to the US to attend Stanford University for computer science.
Worked briefly as a software engineer at Facebook while still a Stanford student.
Co-founded DoorDash with Tony Xu and Andy Fang to solve local restaurant delivery for small businesses.
Graduated Stanford with BS in computer science (HCI focus); DoorDash continued rapid expansion.
DoorDash IPO made Tang a billionaire alongside cofounders.
DoorDash joined the Fortune 500; Tang remained a board-level cofounder focused on product.

name: Reed Hastings
milestone_by_age_26: No material milestone by age 26 found; Bowdoin BA math (1983, age 22), Peace Corps teaching in Swaziland (1983–1985), then Stanford MS CS (1988, age 27). Pure Software founded 1991 (age 30–31); Netflix founded 1997 (age 36–37).
early_history_summary: Born Boston to attorney Wilmot Reed Hastings Sr. (HEW under Nixon) and debutante Joan Amory Loomis (Boston Brahmin lineage, great-grandson of Alfred Lee Loomis). Buckingham Browne & Nichols; Bowdoin math 1983; Marine OCS summer then Peace Corps math teaching in Swaziland; Stanford MS CS 1988 after MIT rejection.
family_context_summary: Upper-class Boston/Cambridge family; father a federal attorney; mother from Boston Brahmin Loomis family who rejected high society; great-grandfather Alfred Lee Loomis was a notable financier-scientist.
parent_family_domain_summary: Elite professional/family network and education pipeline, but not software-industry domain expertise.
evidence_summary: Hastings had elite education and unusual early service (Peace Corps) by his mid-twenties, but software founding success began with Pure Software in 1991 (~age 31) and Netflix in 1997 (~age 37). Stanford MS at 27 already sits past the age-26 line for a technical breakout. No dated material company-building or research milestone by 26 was found.
